incident-bot: Pager — SEV2: smart-routing policy anomaly in us-west-2. Symptoms: incorrect model variants served after fallback, elevated non-deterministic responses. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Start: 2026-03-15T02:12:01Z. Impact: ~10% requests returning wrong-variant outputs. @Erica (oncall) @Ryan (eng-runtime) @Maria (sre)
Erica (oncall): oncall here, grabbing context. tagging support to gather customer impact.
Jordan (support): seeing ~12% of recent requests with mismatched model id in response headers, customers A & C reported content oddities. I can surface logs if needed.
Ryan (eng-runtime): pulling route logs now. initial hunch: KV cache key derivation changed after a rollback of routing-policy config — keys include model_id + region but fallback injects variant token causing key mismatch.
Maria (sre): I'm on infra. checking redis latency/evictions. Could be thundering fallback causing rapid namespace reuse.
Ryan (eng-runtime): logs snippet: ```
[02:11:52] request_id=xyz model=redwood-open-v1 routed_to=redwood-open-v2 kv_key="redwood-open-v1|us-west-2"
[02:11:52] fallback_exec: picked_variant=redwood-open-v2
[02:11:52] cache_lookup returned kv_key="redwood-open-v2|us-west-2" -> hit -> returned state for v2
[02:11:52] response.headers: served-model=redwood-open-v2
```
Ryan (eng-runtime): The problem: the routing layer mutated the key used to lookup cached KV state after fallback selection, causing some requests to use cached KV for a different variant than the route originally intended. So two different formats are now coexisting: `model|region` and `model_variant|region`.
Erica (oncall): immediate mitigation options?
Maria (sre): we can force fallback policy to strict-variant-match (disable auto-variant-fallback) to stop the policy from mutating keys. Also recommend flushing the per-region KV prefix for the affected model to avoid cross-variant reuse.
Ryan (eng-runtime): I can push a config patch to disable fallback mutation. patch: `routing.fallback.mutate_kv_key = false` — will push to canary then global if green.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: routing-config-v2 -> canary us-west-2 (unlock by @Ryan (eng-runtime)).
Ryan (eng-runtime): running command to flush kv prefix for us-west-2/model redwood-open:
```
# careful: deletes only us-west-2/redwood-open prefixes
redis-cli -h kv-usw2 --scan --pattern "us-west-2:redwood-open*" | xargs -r redis-cli -h kv-usw2 del
```
Ryan (eng-runtime): executed flush at 02:14:10Z.
Maria (sre): noticed drop in error spike after flush. redis evictions back to normal.
Jordan (support): Verified customers A & C saw mismatched outputs up until 02:14:20Z; after that responses look correct. I'll send quick notes to affected customers and offer follow-up.
Kate (product): what about data integrity? any persisted state lost that could affect outputs?
Ryan (eng-runtime): flushing KV clears ephemeral KV-prefetch/cache state (prefix caches) — no durable customer data. Still, some in-flight sessions that relied on cached prefix tokens might see a cold start.
Maria (sre): rolling back the routing config patch if anything breaks is ready. have canary metrics wired.
Erica (oncall): handover: @Ryan please lead mitigation, @Maria on infra watch, I'm doing incident comms and will start severity timeline. If mitigation completes, I'll mark resolved and request a postmortem.
Ryan (eng-runtime): canary deploy looks good (02:15:05Z). No increase in latency, error rate returning to baseline. will promote to global in 5m.
deploy-bot: canary -> global promotion scheduled by @Ryan (eng-runtime).
Ryan (eng-runtime): promoted config globally at 02:19:40Z. Observability shows mismatch % dropping from 11.8% -> 0.6% over 5 minutes.
Jordan (support): customer impact summary for support notes: affected customers: A, C (partial); window: 02:11:52Z - 02:14:20Z (mitigated), estimated impacted requests: ~8-13% depending on traffic. No data leak or persisted corruption.
Erica (oncall): incident resolved? initial metrics look healthy. anyone object to marking RESOLVED? :white_check_mark:
Kate (product): note for postmortem: need safety check in routing layer to avoid mutating cache key format post hoc. Also request backlog of canary tests that include fallback scenarios.
Ryan (eng-runtime): root cause draft: routing fallback mutated cached-key namespace format (inconsistent delimiter/tags), causing cross-variant cache hits during fallback loops. Contributing factor: config rollback left inconsistent key format across a small service ring. Fix: enforce canonical KV key generation (server-side) + config guardrails + unit tests for fallback path.
Maria (sre): follow-up ops actions: add alert on cross-variant served-model header mismatch rate, add a short TTL on prefix caches so flushes are less disruptive.
Erica (oncall): assigning postmortem to Ryan and Maria. Will create incident doc and link to this thread. Good work everyone.
Jordan (support): I'll reach out to affected customers and share timeline.
Ryan (eng-runtime): marking mitigation complete at 02:20:45Z. closing loop.
incident-bot: Incident SEV2 resolved by Erica (oncall) at 2026-03-15T02:20:45Z. Postmortem requested.
